title: Kestrel and the Summer
premise: Casper Amberdale keeps her late grandfather's lighthouse on the Cornish coast and writes romance novels she refuses to publish, convinced love is a discipline of the will. When a February storm strands rival vintners Julian Kestrel and Wren Summer — former lovers turned courtroom enemies over a stolen heirloom vine — in her keeper's cottage, Casper becomes unwilling mediator, then confidante, then the woman both men cannot stop thinking about. As the dispute escalates toward a lawsuit that would bankrupt one family, Casper must confront why she fled her own engagement years ago and forgive herself for choosing safety over feeling. At the vineyard's first harvest, she testifies to what she witnessed that winter, the truth frees Julian's family from blame without destroying Wren's, and Casper chooses neither man until she can finally choose herself — after which she chooses Julian, not as rescue but as equal.
about_author: Ivo Vane is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs along the English coast before turning to fiction. They write from a converted signal station, where they insist the fog gives better editorial notes than any agent.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Keeping
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She maintains the lighthouse, catalogs her grandfather's logs, and drafts the ending of her unpublished novel, deleting the kiss scene as 'unrealistic.' Establishes her creed: hearts are muscles, trainable and containable. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: Storm Glass Falling
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Barometer plunges; radio warns of a February gale. She battens the cottage, half-hoping for interruption, hating herself for hoping. A knock at the door as visibility dies. Emotional beat: anticipation disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Two Men, One Doorway
chapters.summary: Julian and Wren arrive soaked and snarling, having shared a broken-down car up the cliff road. Casper recognizes their names from legal headlines: Kestrel v. Summer. POV shifts among all three. Emotional beat: forced intimacy crackling with old wounds.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Stranded indefinitely, he negotiates truce terms at Casper's kitchen table while she watches like a referee who owns the ring. He notices how she deflects every personal question. Emotional beat: curiosity kindled under irritation.

chapters.title: What the Vine Was Worth
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Over bad stew, the rivals' history leaks out: lovers once, then the theft accusation over the Kestrel heirloom cutting that launched Wren's celebrated vineyard. Julian insists on innocence; Wren insists on evidence. Emotional beat: grief wearing armor.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Log
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Reading her grandfather's entries, she finds his own record of a stranded pair decades ago — and his confession of loving one of them. First crack in her creed. Emotional beat: inheritance of an unresolved heart.

chapters.title: Chores and Ceasefires
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. The trio falls into domestic rhythm: Julian repairs the generator, Wren cooks, Casper writes secretly at night. Small kindnesses accumulate like snowdrifts. Emotional beat: found family forming before anyone admits it.

chapters.title: Manuscript in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He finds Casper's manuscript by accident and reads it through the night — recognizing the two rivals in her fictional lovers. He says nothing, but everything about his gaze changes. Emotional beat: being seen without consent, and liking it.

chapters.title: Ice on the Gallery Rail
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian and Casper climb to the lamp room to clear ice; a near-fall ends in his arms. Neither pulls away fast enough. He tells her about the night the cutting vanished and why he never fought the accusation publicly. Emotional beat: vertigo as honesty.

chapters.title: Wren's Version
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tells Casper his side alone: he bought the cutting in good faith from a broker, was framed or fooled, and lost Julian forever anyway. His vulnerability is real and possibly strategic. Emotional beat: sympathy weaponized against itself.

chapters.title: The Mediator's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Both men have now confessed to her; she realizes she is no longer neutral and resents them for it. She drafts a letter to her lawyer sister asking about the case, then burns it. Emotional beat: complicity discovered.

chapters.title: Thaw Warning
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Roads reopen; the storm ends, and nobody leaves. Julian stays 'to finish the generator work.' Wren stays 'to repay hospitality.' Casper lets them, telling herself it's charity. Emotional beat: the excuse everyone accepts because everyone wants it.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Worst Timing
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Julian kisses her in the boathouse; she responds, then stops him cold, citing rules she can't name. She flees to Wren, who offers only silence and tea. Emotional beat: desire colliding with self-protection.

chapters.title: The Sister Arrives
chapters.summary: New POV: Margot, Casper's barrister sister, arrives unannounced, appalled to find her sister hosting both parties to active litigation. She recognizes the manuscript plot instantly. Emotional beat: outside eyes making private weather public.

chapters.title: Conflict Check
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot explains that anything Casper learned could be subpoenaed; her testimony could decide the case. Casper realizes her winter has legal weight. The men go quiet around her. Emotional beat: love as liability.

chapters.title: Harvest Ledger, Old Errors
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Digging into his own records to preempt discovery, Wren finds the broker's invoice is forged — someone inside his operation framed him, or he was careless enough to be framed. Doubt corrodes his certainty. Emotional beat: justice beginning at home.

chapters.title: Julian's Confession Draft
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian writes a letter admitting he suspected his own cousin sold the cutting and stayed silent to protect the family name. He asks Casper whether truth or loyalty comes first. She gives no answer. Emotional beat: the cost of inherited silence.

chapters.title: Mirror Work
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Alone, Casper finally reads her grandfather's final log entry: he chose neither lover and called it wisdom; she calls it cowardice, and hears herself. She begins rewriting her novel's ending honestly. Emotional beat: forgiveness of the person in the mirror, begun.

chapters.title: Rivals at the Table
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Julian shows Wren the forged invoice; Wren shows Julian his broker correspondence. Together they trace the frame to Julian's cousin and Wren's cellar manager, conspiring since the breakup. The enemies' alliance forms. Emotional beat: common enemy, unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: What Casper Saw
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The men realize Casper overheard key confessions during the storm — testimony that could exonerate Wren and implicate the cousin. They ask her to testify. She refuses: she won't be anyone's instrument again. Emotional beat: agency asserted.

chapters.title: Margot's Offer
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot proposes Casper testify voluntarily, shaping the narrative rather than being used by it. Casper wavers; the men, ashamed, withdraw the request entirely, each privately deciding to sacrifice his case rather than her peace. Emotional beat: love demonstrated by restraint.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren invites Julian to help replant the disputed vine row — the cutting's descendants — as a gesture. Julian accepts. Working soil together, old love surfaces as muscle memory. Casper watches from the fence line, excluded and relieved. Emotional beat: grief composted into growth.

chapters.title: Jealousy of a Different Shape
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian sees Wren and Casper laughing over her manuscript and feels something new: not rivalry for her, but fear that the two people he needs most belong to each other instead. Emotional beat: jealousy transmuted into loneliness.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper finds Julian's confession draft and reads it. She also finds Wren's unsent letter to her, declaring feelings he'll never press. Two letters, two loves, zero pressure — and she cracks open anyway, weeping at the kitchen table. Emotional beat: the contained heart overflowing.

chapters.title: Choosing Not to Choose
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper tells both men plainly: she cares for them both, she chooses no one yet, and if that costs her them, so be it. To her shock, they stay — as friends first. The triangle becomes a strange, honest household. Emotional beat: radical honesty as foundation.

chapters.title: Discovery Day
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Legal discovery lands: the cousin's firm subpoenas Casper's storm-season presence regardless. The choice she made is taken from her; she will testify or be held in contempt. Emotional beat: autonomy under siege.

chapters.title: Preparation
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Margot preps Casper; Julian and Wren coach her on facts, each terrified of what cross-examination will do to her. The household tightens around her like a crew before weather. Emotional beat: found family mobilized.

chapters.title: Night Before Court
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Eve of trial. Three chairs on the gallery rail, watching the light turn. No declarations — just Julian's hand on her shoulder, Wren's joke, the beam sweeping. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: The Witness Box
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the stand, Casper testifies to the storm-night confessions with precision and mercy — damning the conspiracy, sparing both men's dignity. Cross-examination turns vicious about her 'relationship' with both parties. Emotional beat: composure as courage.

chapters.title: The Verdict Weather
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The court finds the forgery proven; the cousin settles criminally, Wren's title is cleared, and the Kestrels' counterclaim collapses. Julian loses the lawsuit and gains the truth. Emotional beat: defeat that feels like release.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Cellar Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren fires his cellar manager, then stands in the empty barrel room understanding he built a victory on a lie he half-believed. He writes to Julian: no apology could fit, so he sends a bottle of the first true vintage instead. Emotional beat: accountability without self-destruction.

chapters.title: Cousin's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confronts his cousin before sentencing; the family name is scorched but salvageable. His mother disowns the cousin, not Julian — the first time the family has chosen him. Emotional beat: belonging earned through rupture.

chapters.title: Manuscript, Finished
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper finishes the novel with its real ending: the heroine chooses herself first. She submits it to an agent under a pen name. For the first time, the act of writing feels like testimony rather than hiding. Emotional beat: authorship reclaimed.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Grapes begin coloring; Wren asks Casper — not Julian — to stand with him at harvest as family, nothing more. She accepts. The word 'family' lands softly on all three. Emotional beat: love redefined beyond romance.

chapters.title: Julian's Question
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian asks Casper for nothing except one honest dinner, no witnesses, no storm, no case. She says yes — on her timeline, her terms. He agrees gladly. Emotional beat: patience as devotion.

chapters.title: The Dinner
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. One dinner, one candle, one conversation with no litigation, no legacy, no lighthouse between them. Casper tells Julian about the engagement she fled and why. He listens without fixing. Emotional beat: intimacy without escape routes.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Harvest day: the whole improbable household picks grapes side by side — Margot included, grudgingly charmed. The first press of the season is dedicated to the keeper's log. Emotional beat: abundance as proof of repair.

chapters.title: Offer on the Table
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers Casper not rescue but partnership: co-authorship of a life, her career untouched, his family's mess hers to refuse. She asks for time. He gives it without flinching. Emotional beat: proposal as invitation, not claim.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the lamp room where she nearly fell, Casper decides: not between two men, but between her old containment and this risky, chosen life. She descends the stairs and says yes to Julian — freely, finally, as an equal. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness completed.

chapters.title: Kestrel and the Summer
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating POV. Autumn: the novel publishes to quiet acclaim; the vineyard's first bottles carry a label drawn from the keeper's log; three names — Kestrel, Summer, Amberdale — appear on the dedication page. The light turns above them all. Emotional beat: home as something built, not found.
